items.text: The discovery package (packages/api-core/discovery/resolve.go) is stateless — each call shells out to `vrooli scenario port`. Event emission can wrap ResolveScenarioURL without changing the resolution contract. The CommandRunner interface makes testing straightforward.

Swarm-manager's internal/eventlog/ already implements the exact fire-and-forget SQLite emitter pattern needed. It uses WAL mode, Repository interface abstraction, and non-blocking Emit* methods. This can be generalized into packages/api-core/ as a shared library.

No rate limiting, circuit breaking, or access control middleware exists anywhere in the codebase. Policy enforcement is a completely greenfield design space. The retry/backoff package provides exponential backoff with jitter but is not a policy framework.

Proto infrastructure (buf + packages/proto/schemas/) already generates Go, TypeScript, Python, and JavaScript. Agent-manager's RunEvent proto with oneof discriminated unions provides a template for the vrooli-events envelope. Adding vrooli-events/v1/ follows the established pattern.

items.context: The initiative settled on structured event IDs ({scenario}.{domain}.{action}.{version}) but the full envelope metadata is unspecified. Agent-manager's RunEvent includes id, run_id, sequence, event_type, and timestamp. The vrooli-events envelope needs to carry enough context for policy evaluation, routing, and debugging without bloating every event.

options.label: Minimal envelope: event_id, source_scenario, target_scenario, event_type (structured ID), timestamp, payload (bytes)
options.rationale: Smallest wire size, fastest serialization. Policy evaluation needs only source/target/type. Payload is opaque — consumers deserialize based on event_type.

options.label: Rich envelope: event_id, source_scenario, target_scenario, event_type, timestamp, correlation_id, payload, metadata (map<string,string>)
options.rationale: Adds correlation_id for request tracing across scenarios and a metadata map for extensibility. Moderate overhead. Enables debugging and audit trails without schema changes.

options.label: Full observability envelope: adds span_id, parent_span_id, priority, ttl, retry_count on top of option B
options.rationale: Enables distributed tracing integration and event lifecycle management. Higher overhead but future-proofs for OpenTelemetry integration.

items.context: Policy rules (access control, rate limiting, circuit breaking) need a storage and evaluation format. No existing policy infrastructure exists in the codebase. Rules are cached at both sender-side (discovery package) and receiver-side (middleware). The format must be compact for caching, fast to evaluate, and expressible in proto for SSE push.

options.label: Typed proto messages per policy kind (AccessRule, RateLimit, CircuitBreaker) with enum-based matching
options.rationale: Strong typing, fast evaluation (no parsing), easy to validate at write time. Each rule type has its own fields. Downside: adding a new policy kind requires a proto schema change.

options.label: Generic rule proto with condition/action fields using a simple DSL (e.g., 'source=swarm-manager AND action=backlog.*')
options.rationale: More flexible — new rule types without schema changes. But requires a parser, is harder to validate, and slower to evaluate than typed enums.

options.label: JSON-based rules stored as bytes in proto, evaluated by a rules engine
options.rationale: Maximum flexibility but loses proto type safety. Harder to cache efficiently. Useful if rule complexity will grow beyond what proto types can express.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own policy rule format

items.context: The initiative notes that 'if vrooli-events is unreachable, last-known policy holds (configurable fail-open or fail-closed per rule).' But event emission behavior during outages is unresolved: should senders buffer events locally for later delivery, or drop them? Buffering ensures no event loss but requires local disk/memory, adds complexity, and could grow unbounded during extended outages.

options.label: Drop events during outage, log warning
options.rationale: Simplest. Fire-and-forget means exactly that — if the bus is down, events are lost. Analytics may have gaps but scenario operations are never impacted. Matches the zero-latency requirement strictly.

options.label: Local ring buffer with configurable max size (e.g., 1000 events or 10MB), flush on reconnect
options.rationale: Bounded risk. Events are buffered up to a limit, then oldest are dropped. Adds moderate complexity but prevents total loss during brief outages while protecting against unbounded growth.

options.label: Local SQLite WAL buffer with configurable retention, background flush
options.rationale: Durable buffering survives process restarts. Most complex but guarantees no event loss up to retention limit. May be overkill given fire-and-forget semantics.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own outage handling strategy

items.text: The initiative has 4 items total: this research (architecture design), then execute/vrooli-events-core-runtime, execute/discovery-event-emission-and-policy-cache, and execute/vrooli-events-analytics-ui. This research must produce enough architectural detail for all three execute items to proceed independently.
